image_description: A side-profile view of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor) swimming near a rocky reef structure. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a bright yellow posterior body and tail. The background consists of blurred coral/rock textures and deep blue water.

The caudal fin has a generally rounded shape, consistent with the species.

The diagnostic black margin on the tail is missing or extremely faint, causing the tail to look like a generic yellow shape rather than the specific species trait.
The mouth area is indistinct and lacks the sharpness seen in the eye, failing to resolve the complex 'brush-like teeth' structure.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm if the visual features (color block ratio, body shape) are sufficient for a high-confidence classification as Holocanthus tricolor despite missing micro-details.
To audit the connectivity of the fins to the body and check for 'melting' artifacts where the fins merge with the background or body.
To assess the naturalism of the scales and skin texture, checking for AI-generated smoothness or noise patterns.

focus_areas: Fin ray definition and separation from body
Presence of black margin on caudal fin
Texture consistency of scales vs. fins
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the dorsal fin structure. In real Rock Beauties, the spiny vs. soft ray distinction is subtle but present. AI often smears this into a single triangle. Also, verify the tail margin; the absence of the black edge is a significant taxonomic error even if the main colors are correct.
